items.title: Tom Scott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2022 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I just played them with all these wonderful, again sort of 60s Wrecking Crew musicians. Carol Kaye on bass...

ctx.x: When you got ready to do a solo recording what came first, the band? The material? Or the agreement from a record company?

Well my very first album was for Bob Thiele of Impulse. And he, I figured out that he thought he could make me into kind of a pop saxophone player. I think maybe he thought he could get a pop instrumental hit from my album, my first album. It was called “Honeysuckle Breeze” which was an original tune composed by Ian Freebairn-Smith, one of the arrangers. I basically just walked in and played the charts that were put in front of me. So I guess I had signed the contract with Impulse, a typical record deal at that…
Well there was a time, especially in the 50s and 60s where you could have an instrumental hit, you know “Cast Your Fate to the Wind” and “Stranger on the Shore.”
